plant.cvs: 'Crimson Queen' – red-purple finely cut weeping · 'Garnet' – deep red dissected · 'Viridis' – green finely cut · 'Inaba-shidare' – dark red, larger dissected leaves
plant.hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and Northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C, though young spring growth can be damaged by late frosts.
plant.prune: Little needed. Remove dead, damaged or crossing shoots only when fully dormant (Nov-Jan), because cuts bleed if made in spring.
plant.resilience: Fully hardy once established but leaves brown in drying wind, strong afternoon sun or drought. Pests: aphids; verticillium wilt and coral spot can occur.
plant.soilWarning: Leaves scorch in cold wind and hot sun
sources: RHS guidance on Acer palmatum and the Dissectum group as remembered, not checked online
General horticultural knowledge of Japanese maple culture in the UK, not checked online
uncertain: latin/cultivar: 'Cascade' is not a cultivar I can confidently identify. It may be a trade or descriptive name for a weeping Dissectum-group plant. The label needs checking, and all fields are written at species / weeping-form level until the cultivar is confirmed.
hue: left null because leaf colour (green, red or purple) depends on the cultivar and is unknown.
height and spread: left blank because they are unknown for this cultivar. Weeping dissected forms are typically small, but no figure is given without the label.
hardiness: H6 is the RHS rating for Acer palmatum as remembered. Not verified for this specific cultivar.
peak: Apr-Nov is used as the foliage season. If this cultivar is sold on autumn colour, Oct-Nov may suit better.
foliage: whether the leaves are finely dissected or simply lobed is unknown.
soil/clay: tolerates heavier soils that do not waterlog, but clay suitability is not established, so clay is left blank.

toxicity: no recognised hazard to people or pets for Acer palmatum as remembered. Some other maples (sycamore, red maple) are linked to poisoning in horses, and A. palmatum is not confirmed either way for horses.
compliance: no Schedule 9 listing or breeders' rights known. PBR status cannot be checked without the cultivar identity.
ratings: pestRisk, thirst, careLevel, growthSpeed, sunNeed and sunMin are judged from general Acer palmatum (weeping form) behaviour, not cultivar data.
aspect: East / West is a judgement to avoid harsh midday and afternoon sun and cold north-easterly wind. A sheltered spot matters more than exact facing.
plant.uses: Patio containers · Japanese-style gardens · small gardens · sheltered borders · beside water features
plant.visual: Low, cascading mound of lobed maple leaves · foliage interest spring to autumn, with autumn colour in Oct-Nov
plant.water: Water through dry spells, especially in pots and in its first two summers; keep evenly moist but never waterlogged.
